newsitem.title: CHILE: El Abra still expects to reach capacity in 1997.
newsitem.headline: El Abra still expects to reach capacity in 1997.

text.p: El Abra copper mine expects to reach capacity production in the first half of 1997 as scheduled despite a serious accident last week, but is still studying the accident's impact, a spokesman said.

The mine was expecting to reach capacity-rate production of 500 million pounds of cathodes a year in the first half of 1997 but could not yet rule out a hit to 1997 production levels due to the accident, said spokesman Mike Rounds.
"We're still in a quasi-startup mode, so we're still ramping up to full capacity," said Rounds, spokesman for the mine's owners Cyprus Amax Minerals Co.

"What we've said is first or second quarter of 1997" is when the mine will reach full production, he said. Nothing so far had led the mine's engineers to discard that target, but nor had they finished assessing damage from the accident, he said.
"We just don't know that yet," he said.
Four men died and a key conveyor belt was buried in tonnes of earth and rubble last Wednesday when a tunnel collapsed as workers loaded soil on top of it.
Rounds denied a report in the Santiago newspaper El Mercurio quoting El Abra official John Fenn as saying the mine had only a week's worth of stockpiles.
"That's a very serious misquote ... That is not accurate," he said.
